blocks.text: 1. Attention Masks
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446021409-255649320.png

Causal Masking, the previous topic, covered one genuinely specific, important type of masking. Attention Masks give a broader look at masking beyond just the causal case, closing the Transformers module with a genuinely complete picture.
This closes the Transformers module by generalizing the masking idea to several genuinely different purposes, explored throughout this final topic of the module.
2. Recapping Causal Masking As One Type
This connects back to Causal Masking, already covered in its own topic. Causal Masking, already covered there, is genuinely just one specific, important type of Attention Mask.
This topic genuinely surveys the broader family this technique actually belongs to, placing that earlier, specific technique within its own genuinely wider context.
3. The General Mechanism
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446021410-566884460.png

This connects back to the masking mechanism, already covered in Causal Masking. Every kind of Attention Mask genuinely uses the exact same underlying trick: setting forbidden scores to negative infinity before Softmax.
This is already covered in complete mathematical detail in that earlier topic, meaning every mask type covered throughout the rest of this topic genuinely reuses that exact same technique.

blocks.text: 4. The Padding Mask, Explained
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446021410-202773081.png
This connects back to padding for sequences, already covered in Time Steps. A padding mask genuinely prevents Attention from attending to genuinely artificial filler positions.

This is added specifically to make genuinely variable-length sequences fit into a uniform batch, already covered there, giving that earlier padding technique its own genuinely necessary Attention-side companion.
5. Why Padding Genuinely Needs Masking

A genuinely important, real practical problem connects back to padding tokens carrying genuinely no real information, already covered generally. Without masking, already covered in this topic, the network could genuinely waste attention on these meaningless filler positions.
This genuinely real, practical problem, already covered in this section, directly motivates the padding mask already covered in the previous section as a genuinely necessary safeguard.

blocks.title: warning
blocks.content: Forgetting a padding mask, already covered in this topic, is a genuinely common, real implementation mistake, since padding tokens can otherwise genuinely receive meaningful attention weights despite carrying no real, useful information at all.

blocks.text: 6. Combining Multiple Masks
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446021411-689106.png
This connects back to Causal Masking and padding masks, both already covered. A genuinely single Attention computation can genuinely combine both a causal mask and a padding mask together.

This works by simply adding their genuinely respective negative infinity values together before Softmax, a genuinely elegant, direct way of enforcing multiple genuinely separate constraints simultaneously.
7. Encoder Masking, Revisited
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446021808-879356959.png
This connects back to the encoder does not need this, already covered in Causal Masking. The encoder genuinely still needs padding masks, even though it genuinely never needs causal masking.
This is a genuinely important, real distinction worth stating explicitly in this topic, since "no masking at all" and "no causal masking specifically" are genuinely different, easily confused claims.

blocks.text: 8. Cross-Attention Masking
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446021810-259390311.png
This connects back to Cross-Attention, already covered in its own topic. Cross-Attention genuinely also needs a padding mask, applied to the encoder's own output this time.
This prevents the decoder from genuinely attending to the encoder's own filler positions too, extending the padding mask idea already covered throughout this topic to this genuinely third context.
9. Recognizing When Different Attention Masks Are Genuinely Necessary

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Different Attention Masks Are Genuinely Necessary
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446021810-292917360.png

This connects back to batching genuinely variable-length sequences together, already covered in this topic. Padding masks, already covered in this topic, are genuinely required in almost every real, practical training setup.
This connects back to decoder Self-Attention, already covered in Causal Masking. Causal masks, already covered, remain genuinely essential there specifically.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates combining a causal mask and a padding mask together in a single Attention computation, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

sequence_length = 5
actual_length = 3  # already covered as padding for sequences, the rest is genuinely padding
rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
raw_scores = rng.normal(size=(sequence_length, sequence_length))

# already covered as visualizing the triangular mask in Causal Masking
causal_mask = np.triu(np.ones((sequence_length, sequence_length)), k=1).astype(bool)

# already covered as the padding mask, explained in this topic
padding_mask = np.zeros((sequence_length, sequence_length), dtype=bool)
padding_mask[:, actual_length:] = True  # genuinely forbid attending to padded positions

combined_mask = causal_mask | padding_mask  # already covered as combining multiple masks in this topic
masked_scores = raw_scores.copy()
masked_scores[combined_mask] = -np.inf

def softmax(x):
    exp_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    return exp_x / exp_x.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)

attention_weights = softmax(masked_scores)
print("Combined causal and padding attention weights:")
print(np.round(attention_weights, 3))
print(f"\nNotice columns {actual_length} onward genuinely receive zero attention everywhere, already covered as the padding mask in this topic")

blocks.content: Running this example shows both the upper-right causal region and the padding columns genuinely receiving zero attention weight, exactly the combined masking already covered in this topic.

blocks.text: 11. Transformers: Module Complete

items: Attention Masks generalize masking beyond just the causal case covered in the previous topic.
Every mask type uses the same underlying trick: negative infinity scores before Softmax.
A padding mask prevents attention to artificial filler positions added for batching.
Without masking, the network could waste attention on meaningless padding positions.
A causal mask and a padding mask can be combined in a single Attention computation.
The encoder still needs padding masks, even though it never needs causal masking.
Cross-Attention also needs a padding mask, applied to the encoder's own output.
Padding masks are required almost universally; causal masks are needed specifically in decoder Self-Attention.
